title: Founding the band amid Miller imitations
summary: Irv Denken and the secondary Miller band fashion, the name, RCA.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis

blocks.x: So he got the musical and I guess it was a disaster because nobody could find anybody, which you just can't do in a show. Just about that time, it began the rage of the secondary Miller bands, everybody was having one.

Irv Denken was the trombone player in McKinley's band, got to be at this point a booker with Willard Alexander, although he was still playing trombone, and he picked up on the idea of the two of us going into the thing, his wife jumped on it and we pushed to the point where it was suggested that somebody approach the record companies and see how they would like it.
Both Columbia and RCA did, and for some reason we went with RCA. We wanted one of those composite titles,

like the who or what, just as long as our names weren't involved in it, but we must have spent six months going through a thousand of these things,and some of them were pretty good, but the brass wouldn't accept it. So we wound up being Sauter-Finegan; that was their choice. We got tagged with it, which meant we had to go on the road, which was a disaster.
